slides.heading: Sort Stack
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Sort Stack, a medium stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Sort a stack (list, top = end) ascending using only push/pop/peek and recursion.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Sort a stack (list, top equals end) ascending using only push or pop or peek and recursion.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Recursively pop to empty, then insert each value back in sorted position.
slides.narration: Recursively pop to empty, then insert each value back in sorted position.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Recursion only (no extra structures) → O(n²) time, O(n) call stack
slides.narration: With only stack operations, this is insertion sort: sort the rest recursively, then insert the top into place. That's quadratic time and linear recursion depth.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Pop the top and sort the rest
slides.narration: Step by step. First, pop the top and sort the rest. Second, insert it back. Third, insertion pops larger tops temporarily.

slides.caption: Recursively pop until empty
slides.narration: Sort stack pops the top and recursively sorts the rest, until the stack is empty.

slides.narration: Unwinding, insert -5: pop larger tops, place it, and push them back.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Sort stack removes the top, sorts the rest, and inserts the top. Insert adds the value if the stack is empty or the top is smaller or equal; otherwise it removes the top, inserts recursively and pushes the top back.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n recursion.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Insert pops while the top is bigger than the value, places it, and pushes the popped values back.
